subject: Biotechnology
title: Prime Editing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Prime Editing.

hook.text: Prime editing is the search-and-replace of genetics — it can make any small change without cutting both strands.

buildup.text: A modified Cas9 nicks one strand while a reverse transcriptase writes the new sequence directly into the DNA.

discovery.text: Prime editing can insert, delete, or swap any combination of bases — covering all 12 possible point mutations.

twist.text: Efficiency is still lower than standard CRISPR — making it work well in living organisms remains a challenge.

climax.text: Prime editing could theoretically correct 89% of known disease-causing mutations — the ultimate precision tool.

punchline.text: Search, find, rewrite — prime editing is gene editing's word processor.

quiz.question: What advantage does prime editing have over base editing?
options: It works faster and is more efficient in all cell types
It can make any small insertion, deletion, or substitution, not just single-base swaps
It does not require any guide RNA to find its target

details.summary: Prime editing performs precise insertions, deletions, and all 12 types of point mutations without double-strand breaks or donor DNA templates. A modified Cas9 nickase fused to a reverse transcriptase uses an engineered guide RNA to write new genetic information directly at the target site.
details.whyItMatters: Prime editing has been called a search-and-replace for the genome. It corrects mutations more precisely than CRISPR cutting or base editing, potentially addressing up to 89 percent of known pathogenic mutations while minimizing unwanted editing
takeaways: Prime editing makes precise edits without double-strand DNA breaks
It can perform insertions, deletions, and all 12 point mutation types
Potentially corrects up to 89 percent of known disease-causing mutations

faq.question: How does prime editing write new genetic information?
faq.answer: A Cas9 nickase cuts one DNA strand while a fused reverse transcriptase uses an extended guide RNA as a template to synthesize new DNA directly at the cut site. The cell incorporates this new sequence, replacing the original. No double-strand break or donor template is needed.

faq.question: What advantages does prime editing have over base editing?
faq.answer: Base editing can only make four types of base-to-base conversions. Prime editing makes all 12 point mutations plus insertions up to about 40 bases and deletions up to about 80 bases. It does not require a PAM directly at the edit site and avoids bystander editing of nearby bases.
